source.title: InputDSA : Demixing then comparing recurrent and externally driven dynamics
source.authors: Ann C. Huang; Mitchell Ostrow; S. H. Singh; L. Kozachkov; I. Fiete; Kanaka Rajan

record.tranche_reason: The study measures similarity of recurrent dynamics, not convergence of representational distances or any of the specific representation behaviors in V1–V7. Its RNN findings are related but do not test the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper distinguishes dynamical similarity from geometry and applies InputDSA to RNN dynamics. The Plume Tracking results below are recorded as related findings under none; they do not measure representational alignment. The paper also reports singular values of input operators and neural-data results, which do not measure the claim's versions.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper introducing InputDSA, which compares estimated linear dynamics operators (intrinsic A, input B) across systems. It cites the Platonic Representation Hypothesis only as an example of cross-system similarity research. Its RNN results compare dynamical operators among RL plume-tracking agents. They do not measure representational alignment, shared features or subspaces, stitching or mapping, or universal features, and they do not vary model scale or modality. The Top vs Bottom finding (successful agents have similar input-driven dynamics, failed agents are diverse) is a related construct, kept in fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors' main conclusion is methodological: InputDSA robustly compares intrinsic and input-driven dynamics under partial observation and noisy or surrogate inputs. Applied to the plume-tracking RNNs, it shows high performers are dynamically similar and low performers diverse. Applied to rat neural data, it shows a shift from input-driven to intrinsic dynamics at decision commitment.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces InputDSA, comparing estimated intrinsic and input operators rather than representational distances. It uses DSA as a methodological starting point, but does not reproduce the original representation-convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: The study compares intrinsic and input-driven dynamics and reports different patterns for Top and Bottom agent groups and over training.

fits_no_version.finding: Among 15 RL-trained plume-tracking RNNs, the 5 Top agents had significantly more similar input-driven dynamics (InputDSA) than the 5 Bottom agents. Intrinsic dynamics did not differ significantly between groups. Over training, Top agents converged to consistent input-driven dynamics while Bottom agents diverged ('Anna Karenina principle').
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Among task-trained recurrent agents, high-performing networks converge to similar input-driven dynamics while low-performing networks remain heterogeneous.

record.problems: The relevant Plume Tracking outcomes are presented in figures without numerical distances in the text. The study uses five agents per selected performance group; the text does not give a numerical significance test or p-value for the similarity comparisons.

untested.parts: All of it: model scale and capability, and different architectures, objectives or data.
All of it: no vision-language paired data.
Shared features or subspaces across seeds. The plume agents are independently trained, but only dynamical operators are compared, not features.
All of it: no mapping or stitching between models' representations.
Metric dependence of representational convergence. The robustness analyses concern dynamical metrics under input noise, not representational similarity.

record.verdict_notes: Huh et al. 2024 appears only in the first intro sentence as an example, so the relation is 'cites_only' rather than 'discusses'. The performance-linked convergence of dynamics loosely echoes V1's 'better models converge' idea. However, it concerns same-architecture RL agents' dynamical operators, not representations across scale, so no verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: Model size and capability scaling; representational alignment across independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities.
Alignment of vision and language representations of paired images and captions as model performance changes.
Shared features or subspaces across random seeds; the study compares dynamical operators, not features or representational subspaces.
Mapping or stitching representations, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Dependence of representational convergence on similarity metrics, settings, or input data.
Whether representational alignment is incomplete, plateaus, or is explained by shared data or objectives.
